concerns.text: T012.0.2 (Generate sample_list.csv) depends on T012.0.0.5 (Implement Data Streaming Logic), but T012.0.0.5 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) and listed after T012.0.2 in the task list. A consumer (T012.0.2) cannot run before its producer (T012.0.0.5) is implemented. The [P] tag is invalid here as T012.0.0.5 is a hard prerequisite.

T012.0.2 depends on T012.0.1 (Define sampling strategy), but T012.0.1 is marked [P] and appears after T012.0.2 in the list. The sampling strategy logic must exist before the sample list can be generated. This violates producer-before-consumer ordering.

T012.2.1 (Implement selection logic) depends on T012.0.4 (Verify class balance), but T012.0.4 depends on T012.0.2. The chain is T012.0.2 -> T012.0.4 -> T012.2.1. However, T012.0.4 is marked [P] and placed after T012.2.1 in the list, creating a semantic ordering violation where a task appears before its dependency.

T014.2 (Integrate memory chunking) depends on T014 (Implement wrapper), but T014 is marked [X] (complete) while T014.2 is not. However, T014.2 is listed *after* T012.1 (Extract features), which explicitly depends on T014.2. This creates a circular dependency: T012.1 needs T014.2, but T014.2 is scheduled after T012.1. T014.2 must precede T012.1.

T013 (Implement torch.no_grad() inference) depends on T012.1, but T012.1 depends on T014.2. T014.2 depends on T014. T014 is marked complete, but T014.2 is not. The ordering places T013 after T012.1, which is correct, but the dependency chain T012.1 -> T014.2 -> T014.3 (Generate memory log) is broken. T014.3 depends on T014.2, but T014.3 is listed after T017 (Add logging), which also depends on T014.2. The memory log generation (T014.3) must happen during extraction (T012.1/T013), not after T017.

T036 (Main Pipeline) depends on T036.3.1 (Prior Audit), but T036.3.1 depends on T021.4 (Apply Synthetic Perturbations) and T020 (Depth Estimation). T021.4 is listed after T023.1 (Generate labels), which is incorrect. The perturbation (T021.4) must happen BEFORE the labeling (T023.1) because T023.1 labels based on the perturbation status. The current order T023.1 -> T021.4 is a fatal semantic violation.

T023.1 (Generate ground-truth labels) depends on T021.4 (Apply Synthetic Perturbations), but T021.4 is listed *after* T023.1. The labels cannot be generated based on a perturbation that hasn't been applied yet. T021.4 must precede T023.1.

T024 (Separate low-confidence samples) depends on T023.2, which depends on T023.1. T023.1 depends on T021.4. T021.4 is listed after T023.1. This entire chain is broken. T021.4 must be moved before T023.1, and T023.1 before T023.2, and T023.2 before T024.

T030.1 (Filtering logic) depends on T024 (Separate samples), but T024 is listed after T025 (Save valid labels). T025 depends on T024. The order T024 -> T025 is correct, but T030.1 is listed after T031 (Train classifier), which depends on T030.1. T030.1 must precede T031.

T036.3.1 (Prior Audit) depends on T020 (Depth Estimation) and T021.4 (Perturbations). T020 is in Phase 4, T021.4 is in Phase 4. T036.3.1 is in Phase 5. This is correct. However, T036 (Main Pipeline) depends on T036.3.1, but T036 is listed *before* T036.3.1 in the task list. T036.3.1 must precede T036.

T012.0.0.5 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but has a hard dependency on T012.0.0 (Verify Data Source). While T012.0.0 is a prerequisite, the [P] tag implies it can run in parallel with other tasks, but it cannot run in parallel with T012.0.2 which depends on it. The [P] tag is misleading in this context.
T012.0.1 is marked [P] but depends on T012.0.0. Similar to T012.0.0.5, the [P] tag is misleading as it cannot run in parallel with tasks that depend on it (T012.0.2).
